# The Six Controls — A Self-Assessment

> A free, three-minute self-assessment that scores a software team's governance of
> AI-assisted development across six controls. Published by Resolute Software.
> No sign-up is required to take the assessment or see the result.

## What this is

An interactive scorecard at https://ai-scorecard.resolutesoftware.com/ for engineering
leaders, CTOs and heads of software — particularly in regulated industries — who want to
know whether their team's use of AI coding tools is actually governed, and which gap to
close first. Score each of the six controls from 1 to 4, for a total out of 24.

## The six controls

1. **Human ownership & sign-off.** A person owns and signs off on every change AI helps
   write. Ask yourself: could you say who approved a given piece of AI-generated code?
2. **Model strategy & neutrality.** You stay free to switch AI models instead of locking
   into one vendor. Ask yourself: if your main AI provider changed its price or terms, how
   fast could you move?
3. **Developer platform & tooling.** A defined set of approved AI tools, not a free-for-all.
   Ask yourself: do you know every AI tool your developers actually use?
4. **Quality assurance.** More AI-written code means more testing and review, not less.
   Ask yourself: has your testing kept pace with the extra code AI produces?
5. **Security & compliance.** Your AI controls are enforced and recorded, so you can show
   an auditor. Ask yourself: could you show evidence of your AI controls this quarter?
6. **Data governance.** You decide what data AI tools can see, and you can prove it.
   Ask yourself: do you know where your prompt data goes and how long it is kept?

## Scoring scale

Each control is scored on a four-level maturity scale:

- **1 — Ad hoc.** No shared practice.
- **2 — Emerging.** Some practice, inconsistent.
- **3 — Defined.** Documented and mostly followed.
- **4 — Governed.** Enforced and evidenced.

Totals out of 24 fall into three bands:

- **Early (6–12).** AI is running ahead of your governance. Close the security, testing and
  data gaps before an audit or an incident does it for you.
- **Forming (13–19).** The pieces exist but are not yet consistent or provable. Your
  exposure sits in the gaps between them.
- **Governed (20–24).** Ahead of most teams. The work now is keeping it evidenced as your
  models and people change.

Whatever the total, the lowest-scoring control is where to start.

## Statistics cited, with sources

- More than 80% of developers now use AI to write code. Source: Stack Overflow 2025
  Developer Survey, https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai — 84% of 49,000+ respondents
  use or plan to use AI tools; 80.8% use them today, and 51% of professional developers
  use them daily.
- In 45% of cases, an AI model introduces a known security flaw into the codebase when no
  security guidance is given. Source: Veracode Spring 2026 GenAI Code Security Update,
  https://www.veracode.com/blog/spring-2026-genai-code-security/ — 80 coding tasks across
  Java, JavaScript, C# and Python, evaluated across 150+ models. The security pass rate has
  stayed near 55% for two years while models improved in other respects.
